name: ot
label: Occupational therapy document forms
description: ICBC and WorkSafeBC occupational-therapy supplier forms (PDF and Word) prepared for filling. Each form ships with its untouched supplier document.

guidance.purpose: The occupational therapist's first report to ICBC after the initial assessment: diagnosis, current status, limitations, function, treatment goals and the requested program.
guidance.audience: Completed and signed by the treating OT; read by the ICBC recovery specialist who approves treatment.
tips: Dates print as dd/Mmm/yyyy; still submit them as yyyy-MM-dd.
The header carries claim number, dates of accident and report, payee and practitioner details — take these from the referral and the practice profile, never from memory.
Yes/No questions gate the box beneath them: answer the gate, then the detail box, and leave both blank when the topic did not come up.
Symptom, limitation and functional-ability checklists are independent checkboxes; tick every one that applies, not just the first.
The Work and study status and Critical job demands tables are repeating rows — build each row from its `table` object, not from labels.
Narrative boxes are read by an ICBC recovery specialist: state findings and their functional effect, in the third person, without speculation about causation.
Up to four dates of assessment are separate questions — one per visit, in order.
Question 3 medication source is two checkboxes (prescription bottle review, client report), not either/or.
Treatment goals and action steps is a table: goal, action step and timeframe per row.
The Expenses table and the services request (hours, rehabilitation assistant visits) are what ICBC authorises — fill them from the plan, not from the narrative.

guidance.purpose: Progress update to ICBC partway through an approved OT program: what changed since the previous report and what is still requested.
tips: Dates print as dd/Mmm/yyyy; still submit them as yyyy-MM-dd.
The header carries claim number, dates of accident and report, payee and practitioner details — take these from the referral and the practice profile, never from memory.
Yes/No questions gate the box beneath them: answer the gate, then the detail box, and leave both blank when the topic did not come up.
Symptom, limitation and functional-ability checklists are independent checkboxes; tick every one that applies, not just the first.
The Work and study status and Critical job demands tables are repeating rows — build each row from its `table` object, not from labels.
Narrative boxes are read by an ICBC recovery specialist: state findings and their functional effect, in the third person, without speculation about causation.
Date of previous assessment and number of treatment sessions to date anchor the report — take them from the record, not the transcript.
Pre-accident and current function are paired boxes; describe both so the change is visible.
'If no, provide additional information' boxes follow goal-met questions; fill them only when the answer was No.

guidance.purpose: Closing report to ICBC at the end of OT involvement: outcomes against goals, remaining limitations and any recommendations.
tips: Dates print as dd/Mmm/yyyy; still submit them as yyyy-MM-dd.
The header carries claim number, dates of accident and report, payee and practitioner details — take these from the referral and the practice profile, never from memory.
Yes/No questions gate the box beneath them: answer the gate, then the detail box, and leave both blank when the topic did not come up.

Narrative boxes are read by an ICBC recovery specialist: state findings and their functional effect, in the third person, without speculation about causation.
Number of OT visits and RA/KIN visits are totals for the whole program.
Summary/Analysis is the box ICBC reads first: outcome, residual limitation, and whether further services are recommended.

guidance.purpose: A one-page request to ICBC for additional OT treatment hours beyond the initial allocation.
tips: Hours completed, additional hours requested and approved hours remaining are three separate numbers; do not derive one from the others.
Practitioner / Therapist Type has a single option, Occupational Therapy.
Contact preference is a two-state choice; send the option text from the schema.
Anticipated end date is the date the requested block would finish.

guidance.purpose: ICBC's standard invoice for health-provider time and expenses on a claim.
guidance.audience: Prepared by the practice; paid by ICBC against the claim number.
tips: Time charges and Expenses and disbursements are repeating tables: one service date, description, hours or sessions, rate and GST per row, built from the `table` object.
Rates and amounts are numbers; the invoice total is recomputed from the rows.
Vendor and payee details come from the practice profile; the claim number and date of MVA from the referral.

guidance.purpose: Report of a job-site visit: the worker's job demands measured on site, findings, and recommendations to support return to work.
guidance.audience: OT or kinesiologist who made the visit; WorkSafeBC case manager and the employer's RTW contact.
tips: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd in the document itself; submit yyyy-MM-dd.
Header fields (claim number, worker name, date of injury, area and nature of injury accepted on claim) come from the WorkSafeBC referral — copy them exactly.
Either/or answers are separate checkboxes with nothing stopping both: tick exactly one.
Distinguish compensable from non-compensable findings wherever the label asks for it; WorkSafeBC officers read for that split.
Recommendations for equipment or additional sessions must have been discussed with the WorkSafeBC officer before the report is submitted — record the date and officer's name where the form asks.
Session counts are numbers; leave them blank rather than guessing when the transcript does not state them.
Strength, Physical and Cognitive demands are tables with frequency, distance or duration columns per demand — fill the row for each demand observed.
Provider travel time and distance are numbers used for billing; take them from the visit record.
List every participant with their role; the report is often shared with the employer.

guidance.purpose: A week-by-week graduated return-to-work schedule agreed with the worker and employer.
guidance.audience: Written by the OT; signed off by WorkSafeBC and shared with the employer.
tips: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd in the document itself; submit yyyy-MM-dd.
Header fields (claim number, worker name, date of injury, area and nature of injury accepted on claim) come from the WorkSafeBC referral — copy them exactly.
Either/or answers are separate checkboxes with nothing stopping both: tick exactly one.
Distinguish compensable from non-compensable findings wherever the label asks for it; WorkSafeBC officers read for that split.
Recommendations for equipment or additional sessions must have been discussed with the WorkSafeBC officer before the report is submitted — record the date and officer's name where the form asks.
Session counts are numbers; leave them blank rather than guessing when the transcript does not state them.
Each week is its own table: week commencing, hours per day (Monday to Sunday), tasks to perform, tasks not to perform, comments.
Hours are numbers per day, not totals; leave days off blank.
Revision number increments on every reissued plan.

guidance.purpose: Word version of the fast-track WorkSafeBC pre-authorisation for durable medical equipment or services.
guidance.audience: Requested by the OT or supplier; approved by the WorkSafeBC officer.
tips: Line items are repeating table rows: answer one row at a time using the `table` object (table name, row, column), never the `· item N` suffix alone.
Prices are numbers; `$1,250.50` is accepted. Totals, GST and PST are recomputed from the rows unless recalculation is turned off.
Delivery dates and item descriptions belong on the same row as their price.
Leave a row entirely blank rather than half-filling it.
Each equipment or service item is a row: description with item or part number, quantity and price.
Comments should state why the request is time-sensitive.

guidance.audience: Treating OT; WorkSafeBC officer and the claim owner.
tips: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd in the document itself; submit yyyy-MM-dd.
Header fields (claim number, worker name, date of injury, area and nature of injury accepted on claim) come from the WorkSafeBC referral — copy them exactly.
Either/or answers are separate checkboxes with nothing stopping both: tick exactly one.
Distinguish compensable from non-compensable findings wherever the label asks for it; WorkSafeBC officers read for that split.
Recommendations for equipment or additional sessions must have been discussed with the WorkSafeBC officer before the report is submitted — record the date and officer's name where the form asks.

The RTW section must be completed whenever the referral included RTW, even if no attempt was made — say so in the 'Other' box.
If equipment rental continues past discharge, give the reason and the follow-up plan where the note asks.

guidance.purpose: Interim OT report to WorkSafeBC requesting the next block of sessions: progress against goals, plan and dates.
tips: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd in the document itself; submit yyyy-MM-dd.

Short-term and long-term goals are separate boxes; the long-term box is only for goals that differ.
Record the date of communication with the WorkSafeBC officer and their name; without it the plan cannot be approved.

tips: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd in the document itself; submit yyyy-MM-dd.
Header fields (claim number, worker name, date of injury, area and nature of injury accepted on claim) come from the WorkSafeBC referral — copy them exactly.
Either/or answers are separate checkboxes with nothing stopping both: tick exactly one.

Session counts are numbers; leave them blank rather than guessing when the transcript does not state them.
Home environment, existing equipment and recommended equipment are three separate boxes; recommendations must already have been discussed with the officer.
The employer contact date is anticipated, not past.
Analysis should separate recovery factors from return-to-work factors.

guidance.purpose: A supplier or OT quote to WorkSafeBC for durable medical equipment, rentals, repairs and delivery.
guidance.audience: Prepared by the supplier or OT; approved by the WorkSafeBC officer.
tips: Line items are repeating table rows: answer one row at a time using the `table` object (table name, row, column), never the `· item N` suffix alone.
Prices are numbers; `$1,250.50` is accepted. Totals, GST and PST are recomputed from the rows unless recalculation is turned off.

guidance.purpose: Assessment of a worker's driving needs and the vehicle modifications or adapted equipment required.
guidance.audience: OT with driver-rehabilitation expertise; WorkSafeBC officer.
tips: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd in the document itself; submit yyyy-MM-dd.
Header fields (claim number, worker name, date of injury, area and nature of injury accepted on claim) come from the WorkSafeBC referral — copy them exactly.
Either/or answers are separate checkboxes with nothing stopping both: tick exactly one.
Distinguish compensable from non-compensable findings wherever the label asks for it; WorkSafeBC officers read for that split.

Diagnosis boxes (paraplegia level, quadriplegia level, amputee, brain injury, other) describe the accepted condition; leave the ones that do not apply blank.
Owned, adapted and proposed vehicle details are separate groups; do not mix years or makes between them.
Control and equipment types are free text next to a checkbox; tick the box and name the type.
Reduced-effort steering and braking are percentages.
